# Flatten the multi-index columns
pivoted_df.columns = pivoted_df.columns.droplevel(0)

# Reset index for easier handling

y = pivoted_df[relevant_series_names[3]]

import pandas as pd

df = pd.read_csv('/data/worldbank_education_gdp.csv')

# Identify the relevant series names
relevant_series_names = [
    'Labor force participation rate, total (percentage of total population ages 15+) (modeled ILO estimate)',
    'School enrollment, primary (percentage gross)',
    'School enrollment, secondary (percentage gross)',
    'Exports of goods and services (annual percentage growth)'
]

# Filter the dataset for the relevant series names
df_filtered = df[df['Series Name'].isin(relevant_series_names)]

# Pivot the data to have years as columns and series names as rows
df_pivot = df_filtered.pivot(index='Country Group', columns='Series Name', values=[col for col in df.columns if col.startswith('19') or col.startswith('20')])

# Flatten the multi-index columns
df_pivot.columns = df_pivot.columns.droplevel(0)

# Reset index for easier handling
df_pivot = df_pivot.reset_index()

# Drop rows with missing values
df_pivot = df_pivot.dropna()

# Display the first few rows of the pivoted data
df_pivot.head()

# Group the data by 'Country Group' and 'Series Name'

# Identify the relevant series names
relevant_series_names = [
    'Labor force participation rate, total (percentage of total population ages 15+) (modeled ILO estimate)',
    'School enrollment, primary (percentage gross)',
    'School enrollment, secondary (percentage gross)',
    'Exports of goods and services (annual percentage growth)'
]

# Filter the grouped data for the relevant series names
filtered_grouped_df = grouped_df[grouped_df['Series Name'].isin(relevant_series_names)]

# Pivot the data to have years as columns and series names as rows
pivoted_df = filtered_grouped_df.pivot(index='Country Group', columns='Series Name', values=[col for col in grouped_df.columns if col.startswith('19') or col.startswith('20')])

# Flatten the multi-index columns
pivoted_df.columns = pivoted_df.columns.droplevel(0)

# Reset index for easier handling

# Drop rows with missing values

y = pivoted_df[relevant_series_names[3]]

# Create a linear regression model

model.fit(X, y)

# Get the coefficients
